sections.heading: Identity and current status
sections.body:
- Project ID: `grok-build`
- Canonical name: Grok Build (`grok`) (`claim-grok-build-sf-identity`, `claim-grok-build-sf-identity-docs`, `claim-grok-build-sf-identity-site`)
- Vendor: SpaceXAI on the LICENSE; X.AI LLC on the changelog footer (`claim-grok-build-sf-vendor`, `claim-grok-build-sf-vendor-llc`)
- Current status: current shipping product (`claim-grok-build-sf-status`)
- Last source-backed identity check: 2026-08-15
- Canonical URL: https://x.ai/build (`claim-grok-build-sf-canonical-url`)
- Public repository: https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build (`claim-grok-build-sf-repository-url`); official open-source page links the same GitHub path (`claim-grok-build-sf-repository-url-oss`)
- Version keep-both: changelog latest **v1.0.3** dated 2026-08-12 (`claim-grok-build-sf-version`); crate `xai-grok-version` on main **1.0.4** (`claim-grok-build-sf-version-crate`). GitHub Releases is empty (`claim-grok-build-sf-no-github-releases`)

sections.heading: What it is and is not
sections.body:
- What it is: SpaceXAI's first-party terminal coding-agent harness and TUI, with headless `-p` and ACP `grok agent stdio` (`claim-grok-build-sf-identity`, `claim-grok-build-sf-identity-docs`)
- What it is not: GitHub names this repo Grok Build (`claim-grok-build-sf-what-it-is-not`); plugin-cc is a Claude Code bridge (`claim-grok-build-sf-what-it-is-not-plugin-cc`); community `grok-cli` is not affiliated with xAI Corp (`claim-grok-build-sf-what-it-is-not-community-cli`); Grok Bot is a separately linked cloud-computer product (`claim-grok-build-sf-what-it-is-not-grok-bot`). Discovery keep-apart: this repo is this id (`claim-grok-build-sf-not-duplicate`); plugin-cc is corpus id `grok-build-cli` (`claim-grok-build-sf-not-duplicate-plugin-cc`); Superagent is corpus id `grok-cli` (`claim-grok-build-sf-not-duplicate-community-cli`)

sections.heading: Architecture and agent-loop ownership
sections.body:
- Primary type: `runtime` (`claim-grok-build-sf-primary-type`)
- Agent-loop owner: Grok Build / `xai-grok-shell` (`claim-grok-build-sf-agent-loop`)
- Architecture: Rust workspace with pager TUI, shell runtime, tools, and workspace crates, synced from the SpaceXAI monorepo (`claim-grok-build-sf-architecture`, `claim-grok-build-sf-lineage-monorepo`)

sections.heading: Surfaces and execution location
sections.body:
- Surface IDs: `surface-grok-build-tui`, `surface-grok-build-headless`, `surface-grok-build-acp`, `surface-grok-build-ssh-generic`
- Execution location: local user machine / project directory (`claim-grok-build-sf-execution-location`)

sections.heading: Model/auth/provider strategy
sections.body:
- Model strategy: marketed as powered by Grok 4.6; custom models via `~/.grok/config.toml`; settings example default id `grok-build` (`claim-grok-build-sf-model-strategy`)
- Auth strategy: browser/OAuth at auth.x.ai, device-code, `XAI_API_KEY`, enterprise OIDC, external auth provider (`claim-grok-build-sf-auth`)
- Provider support: xAI default plus OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic Messages custom endpoints (`claim-grok-build-sf-provider-support`)

sections.heading: Context, memory, compaction, and session behavior
sections.body:
- Context behavior: AGENTS.md family and Claude Code instruction files (`claim-grok-build-sf-context`); `grok inspect` discovered-config wording (`claim-grok-build-sf-context-inspect`)
- Memory: optional cross-session memory, default off (`claim-grok-build-sf-memory`); `--experimental-memory` and `grok memory clear` (`claim-grok-build-sf-memory-cli`); `/remember`, `/memory`, `/flush`, `/dream` when enabled (`claim-grok-build-sf-memory-commands`)
- Compaction: manual `/compact` and auto-compact (`claim-grok-build-sf-compaction`); `auto_compact_threshold_percent` default 85 (`claim-grok-build-sf-compaction-threshold`)
- Session behavior: disk-backed `~/.grok/sessions` with resume, continue, fork, rewind, compact, todos (`claim-grok-build-sf-session-behavior`). Rewind file-restore wording on the Sessions page disagrees with changelog v1.0.1 (`claim-grok-build-sf-rewind-docs`, `claim-grok-build-sf-rewind-changelog`)

sections.heading: Tools, extensions, MCP, skills, hooks, and APIs
sections.body:
- Tools: codebase read/edit, shell, web search, long-running tasks (`claim-grok-build-sf-tools`)
- Extensions: plugins and marketplaces (`claim-grok-build-sf-extensions`)
- MCP: `grok mcp add`, config.toml, `/mcps` (`claim-grok-build-sf-mcp`)
- Skills: `SKILL.md` folders and slash-command skills (`claim-grok-build-sf-skills`)
- Hooks: lifecycle scripts from `~/.grok/hooks`, project hooks, plugins (`claim-grok-build-sf-hooks`)
- APIs: ACP JSON-RPC via `grok agent stdio` (`claim-grok-build-sf-api`)

sections.heading: Orchestration and parallelism
sections.body:
- Orchestration: Rhai workflows of subagents (`claim-grok-build-sf-orchestration`). Subagent default-on docs disagree with `GROK_SUBAGENTS` default `0` (`claim-grok-build-sf-subagents-docs-default`, `claim-grok-build-sf-subagents-env-default`)
- Parallelism: parallel subagents with optional git worktrees (`claim-grok-build-sf-parallelism`, `claim-grok-build-sf-worktrees`)

sections.heading: Isolation, permissions, security, and data path
sections.body:
- Isolation: optional Landlock/Seatbelt sandbox, off by default (`claim-grok-build-sf-isolation`)
- Permissions: ask / auto / always-approve plus allow/deny rules (`claim-grok-build-sf-permissions`)
- Security: `~/.grok/auth.json` 0600; sandbox does not permanently protect `~/.ssh`; plan mode does not gate bash writes (`claim-grok-build-sf-security`)
- Data path: `~/.grok/config.toml` or `$GROK_HOME` (`claim-grok-build-sf-data-path`); `GROK_HOME` is home for config, auth, sessions, skills, plugins, and logs (`claim-grok-build-sf-data-path-home`)

sections.heading: Interface inventory plus remote/mobile/background behavior
sections.body:
List each surface from `surfaces.jsonl` separately. Keep native mobile, first-party mobile web, first-party messaging, vendor relay, remote client, private-network, Termux/mobile terminal, and generic remote shell routes distinct.

- Interface and surface IDs:
  - Interactive TUI: `surface-grok-build-tui` (`claim-grok-build-sf-surface-tui`)
  - Headless CLI: `surface-grok-build-headless` (`claim-grok-build-sf-surface-headless`)
  - ACP stdio: `surface-grok-build-acp` (`claim-grok-build-sf-surface-acp`)
  - Generic SSH: `surface-grok-build-ssh-generic` (`claim-grok-build-sf-surface-ssh`)
- Remote behavior: generic SSH plus experimental `grok wrap`; no first-party vendor relay on that page (`claim-grok-build-sf-remote-access`); device-code login for headless or remote environments (`claim-grok-build-sf-remote-access-device-auth`)
- Mobile behavior: unknown; opened Grok Build pages do not describe a native iOS or Android app (`claim-grok-build-sf-mobile-access`)
- Background behavior: background commands, monitors, `/loop` (`claim-grok-build-sf-background`)
- First-party messaging: unknown
- Native iOS / Android app: unknown
- First-party mobile web: unknown
- Termux / mobile terminal: unknown
- Generic private-network / Tailscale product: unknown
- First-party desktop app: unknown (changelog names `grok-desktop` as an ACP client only)

sections.heading: Pricing, license, maintenance, and lock-in
sections.body:
- Pricing: current page says try for Free (`claim-grok-build-sf-pricing`); launch post named SuperGrok / X Premium Plus (`claim-grok-build-sf-pricing-launch`)
- License: Apache-2.0 on first-party code (`claim-grok-build-sf-license`)
- Maintenance: internally developed; no external PRs; changelog current (`claim-grok-build-sf-maintenance`, `claim-grok-build-sf-status`)
- Lock-in: default first-party auth/models; custom endpoints documented (`claim-grok-build-sf-lock-in`)
- Availability: public installers for macOS, Linux, Windows (`claim-grok-build-sf-availability`)

sections.heading: Unique edge, meaningful drawbacks, best fit, and not-for
sections.body:
- Unique edge: first-party SpaceXAI terminal coding agent with plan mode, parallel subagents, and skills/plugins/hooks/MCP (`claim-grok-build-sf-unique-value`)
- Meaningful drawbacks: sandbox off by default and credential-path caveats (`claim-grok-build-sf-drawback-sandbox-off`); no external PRs (`claim-grok-build-sf-drawback-no-external-prs`)
- Best fit: documented audience is professional software engineers doing complex work in the terminal (`claim-grok-build-sf-intended-user`). This is not a recommendation.
- Not-for: Grok Bot cloud teammates, a native mobile app, or the community Superagent CLI (`claim-grok-build-sf-not-for`)

claims.claim: Pointer to accepted claim-grok-build-sf-agent-loop: Grok Build owns the loop. Compare enum supported.
claims.notes: draft-from-existing parent=claim-grok-build-sf-agent-loop. Promoted 2026-08-17 as accepted pointer. Wave 2 / site-fill parent accepted.

claims.claim: Pointer to accepted claim-grok-build-gf-gb-relay-host: code.grok.com WebSocket relay. Compare tag vendor-relay.
claims.notes: draft-from-existing parent=claim-grok-build-gf-gb-relay-host. Blocking it leaves sessions local-only. Promoted 2026-08-17 as accepted pointer.

claims.claim: Grok reads a subset of Claude Code managed-settings.json policies (permission rules, MCP server allowlists, some telemetry and feedback flags, and marketplace restrictions), Grok's own /etc/grok/requirements.toml always takes precedence, and Claude's disableBypassPermissionsMode is explicitly not applied to Grok's always-approve mode.
claims.value: {"reads":["permission rules","MCP allowlists","telemetry and feedback flags","marketplace restrictions"],"precedence":"grok requirements.toml wins","not_applied":"disableBypassPermissionsMode"}
claims.notes: Refines the canonical zero-configuration Claude Code compatibility claim: policy inheritance is partial and deliberately excludes the bypass-permissions lock. Claude forceLoginMethod maps to disable_api_key_auth and forceLoginOrgUUID maps to force_login_team_uuid.

claims.claim: Configuration loads from five layers with /etc/grok/requirements.toml highest; values pinned there use a fail-closed mechanism that user config, environment variables, and remote settings cannot override, and [ui] disable_bypass_permissions_mode is honored only from root-owned sources.
claims.notes: The lock blocks --yolo, --permission-mode bypassPermissions, Ctrl+O, /always-approve, the Shift+Tab cycle, and catch-all allow rules. The page adds headless modes dontAsk and acceptEdits beyond the canonical ask/auto/always-approve set.

claims.claim: The Agent Dashboard is a fullscreen overview of every session grouped by state (Needs input, Working, Idle, Inactive, Completed, Failed), opened with Ctrl+backslash, /dashboard, or grok dashboard, and can dispatch prompts to new sessions and answer permission prompts inline.
claims.notes: Grouping and pins persist under [dashboard] in ~/.grok/config.toml; the feature is disabled with enabled = false or GROK_AGENT_DASHBOARD=0.

claims.claim: A dedicated hooks page defines hooks as shell commands or HTTP endpoints configured in JSON at ~/.grok/hooks and <project>/.grok/hooks, with events SessionStart, SessionEnd, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse (the only blocking event), PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, PermissionDenied, Stop, StopFailure, Notification, SubagentStart, SubagentStop, PreCompact, and PostCompact.
claims.notes: Canonical attributed hooks to the skills/plugins page with no event list. The page also reads Claude Code .claude/settings.json and Cursor .cursor/hooks.json hook files, and project hooks require /hooks-trust or --trust with the decision stored in ~/.grok/trusted_folders.toml.

claims.claim: Two enterprise login policies exist: disable_api_key_auth forces interactive IdP login and replaces a first-party xAI API key with the IdP session token at request time, and force_login_team_uuid pins login to one or more team UUIDs and implicitly enables disable_api_key_auth.
claims.notes: Third-party BYOK endpoints keep working under disable_api_key_auth because their base_url is not on x.ai. Enforcement applies to cached tokens and silent refreshes.

claims.claim: Enterprise deployment requires only cli-chat-proxy.grok.com for inference and settings and auth.x.ai for OAuth2/OIDC over HTTPS on port 443, with TLS 1.2 or 1.3 enforced by rustls, root certificates from the OS trust store, and no option to disable TLS.
claims.notes: Canonical security claims covered only local credential-file permissions. Standard proxy environment variables are honored and TLS-inspecting proxies need their CA in the OS trust store.

claims.claim: Grok Build can be installed with npm install -g @xai-official/grok, which the enterprise page presents as an alternative that removes the need to reach x.ai or storage.googleapis.com for binaries.
claims.notes: Canonical recorded only the curl and PowerShell installer scripts. The npm path also removes the in-app grok update host requirement.

claims.claim: The enterprise host table lists code.grok.com for remote session sync, sharing, and WebSocket relay, and states that blocking it leaves sessions local-only and makes share links unavailable.
claims.value: {"host":"code.grok.com","purpose":["remote session sync","sharing","WebSocket relay"],"impact_if_blocked":"sessions stay local-only; share links unavailable"}
claims.notes: Contradicts canonical claim-grok-build-sf-remote-access, which scoped its no-vendor-relay reading to the terminal-support page. Both readings are kept as separate rows: this enterprise page establishes a first-party relay host, so the canonical reading is re-scoped to its own page rather than deleted.

claims.notes: Canonical recorded 7140ec21cc4ec809131b0fa774f4b81d61667084 on 2026-08-15; the periodic sync is observably active.

claims.claim: Under Zero Data Retention, generated video must go to a user-supplied S3-compatible bucket configured in ~/.grok/managed_config.toml, and only the presigned URLs leave the machine while the credentials themselves are never sent to xAI.
